intro: Dublin's perfume scene is small but personal: one serious niche boutique, the Dublin shop of a Galway perfume house, and department stores with the big international niche names. Irish perfumers bottle their wet landscape, so look for moss, fern, gorse, wool, rain, sea air and church incense.

weather.feel: Around 5 to 13 °C, damp, windy and often drizzly. Days are short from November.
weather.wear: Cool, damp air keeps scent close to the skin and burns off fresh citrus quickly. Woody, ambery, incense and soft musky scents last longer and feel cosy. Spray your scarf or coat collar: wool holds scent for days. Go light indoors, since pubs and cafés are small and warm.

smells.name: Gorse
smells.what: Spiky yellow-flowered shrub on Irish hills and coastal paths (Howth Head is close to the city). On a sunny day the flowers smell of coconut and vanilla, and some bloom almost all year.

smells.name: Turf smoke
smells.what: Burning peat (turf) has an earthy, smoky-sweet smell you'll still catch in country pubs and villages. Smoky, peaty notes in perfume and whiskey echo it.

smells.name: Sea air
smells.what: Salt, seaweed and wet stone on the coast at Howth, Dún Laoghaire and Sandymount, the inspiration for most 'Irish sea' colognes.

smells.name: Roasting barley
smells.what: Around St James's Gate the Guinness brewery can fill the air with a toasty, malty smell, like dark bread and coffee.

lookfor.why: Smell the whole Irish line in one stop, especially Róisín Dubh (incense rose) and Báinín (Aran-wool musk).
Landscape scents from County Clare. Its nine-scent sample library is the best-value Irish souvenir for a perfume lover.
The easy, affordable Irish sea cologne in pharmacies and gift shops; a good gift.
Northern Irish eaux de parfum with 15 ml travel bottles that fit the carry-on limit.

lookfor.name: Maison Margiela Replica 'Under the Stars'
lookfor.why: Made by Irish perfumer Méabh McCurtin: labdanum, black pepper, leather and oud. Sold at Brown Thomas and Arnotts.

shops.name: Parfumarija
shops.what: Dublin's niche perfume boutique. The owner trained as a perfumer in Grasse; rare independent houses, a guided smelling tour, and custom scents.

shops.name: Cloon Keen (Powerscourt Townhouse)
shops.address: Powerscourt Townhouse, South William Street, Dublin 2
shops.what: The Galway house's Dublin shop in a Georgian townhouse full of small boutiques.

shops.name: Brown Thomas
shops.what: Ireland's luxury department store: big perfume hall with international niche brands (Le Labo and others).

shops.name: Arnotts
shops.what: Large department store north of the river with a wide perfume and beauty floor.

shops.name: Dublin Airport duty free
shops.what: Last chance for big brands (Le Labo is sold here) and bottles over 100 ml, since you buy them after security.

shops.name: Rituals (Grafton Street)
shops.what: Dutch home and body brand with perfumes, candles and gift sets that match.

shops.name: Rituals (Jervis Centre)
shops.what: Second city-centre Rituals, north of the river.

shops.name: The Perfume Shop (Swords Pavilions)
shops.what: Chain perfume shop near the airport with free gift wrapping and a bottle-recycling discount.

trips.name: Galway: Cloon Keen flagship
trips.what: 21a High Street, in a medieval archway in the old town. About 2.5 hours from Dublin by train or bus, so an easy day trip.

trips.name: The Burren Perfumery, County Clare
trips.what: The perfumery in Carron where the scents are blended and bottled by hand, in the middle of the Burren's limestone landscape. Best combined with a Galway or Cliffs of Moher trip.

tips: Carry-on rule: liquids in 100 ml bottles or smaller in one clear bag. Buy big bottles after security, or pack them in checked luggage wrapped in clothes.
Visitors from outside the EU (Canada included) can usually claim back VAT on goods they take home. Ask the shop for a tax-free form and get it stamped at the airport.
Ask for samples or a paper strip before buying; most niche shops are happy to make you a small decant.
Prices are in euros. The atlas shows Canadian-dollar estimates on each house card.

worn.basis: There's no public sales ranking for Dublin, so this is what Irish shops and the Irish press feature most, not a sales chart. The big designer bestsellers at Boots and Brown Thomas are much the same as in Canada.

items.why: The Irish-made cologne you'll see in pharmacies and gift shops everywhere; a common gift and souvenir.
Báinín, the Aran-wool scent, is the Irish niche perfume the press keeps coming back to.
Irish Leather, from a Paris house with a Tipperary co-founder, is the 'Irish' luxury perfume in duty free.

items.name: Designer favourites
items.why: Big designer names fill Boots, Arnotts and Brown Thomas, as at home. Nothing you need to fly here for.

grab.basis: Things that are hard to find or smell in Canada, or that make sense to buy while you're here.

items.why: Rarely sold outside Ireland. Smell the full line at Powerscourt before buying; the €80 set of three 10 ml bottles fits a carry-on.
Its €45 library of all nine scents (2 ml each) is light, cheap to carry and very Irish.
items.where: Online, or at the perfumery in County Clare

items.why: About €40 for 100 ml at pharmacies; the easy, affordable Irish gift. Pack it in checked luggage (over 100 ml).
Small organic West Cork house; you're unlikely to see it in Canada.
15 ml travel bottles, made for carry-ons.

items.name: European niche at EU prices
items.why: Irish prices include 23% VAT. As a non-EU visitor you can claim part of it back on goods you take home (refund services keep a fee), so compare with the Canadian price before buying at Parfumarija or Brown Thomas.
Bought after security at Dublin Airport, so the 75 ml size isn't stuck at the liquids check.

seasons.name: Autumn
seasons.feel: Shorter, damp days, wet leaves, and Halloween, which grew out of the old Irish festival of Samhain. Expect bonfire smoke on Halloween night, roasting chestnuts and barmbrack, the Irish spiced fruit loaf.
seasons.note: Try Castaña (roasted chestnut) at Cloon Keen and Burren's Autumn Harvest (blackcurrant, hazelnut).

seasons.name: Winter
seasons.feel: Cold, dark and festive: Christmas markets, turf and log fires, mulled wine and church incense at midnight mass.
seasons.note: Róisín Dubh (incense rose) and Burren's Winter Woods (cedar, pine, vetiver) suit it best.

seasons.name: Spring
seasons.feel: Gorse turns the hills yellow and smells of coconut; bluebells fill the woods; St Patrick's Day in March.
seasons.note: Burren's Spring Harvest (mint, lemon balm, fennel) and Cloon Keen's Lá Bealtaine (sunny blossom) fit the season.

seasons.name: Summer
seasons.feel: Long, light evenings, sea swims at the Forty Foot and Howth, meadows of meadowsweet.
seasons.note: Burren's Summer Harvest (meadowsweet, chamomile) and Inis's sea cologne are made for it.

gems.basis: Small or newer names that have had recent attention in the Irish press or at fragrance fairs. 'Buzz' means coverage, not sales.

items.buzz: Named a 'One to Watch' at Pitti Fragranze, and featured by RTÉ and the Irish Times as an organic West Cork house.

items.name: Madigan Rose 27
items.buzz: A fresh rose from an Irish cashmere brand, first made to scent its shops and then released because customers kept asking for it.

items.name: Oxmantown
items.buzz: Roll-on scented oils made by hand by an aromatherapist in a small Stoneybatter studio (jasmine and ylang-ylang, Atlas cedar, lemongrass).

items.name: A custom scent at Parfumarija
items.buzz: The Grasse-trained owner makes bespoke perfumes, a one-off souvenir nobody else has.
Irish Leather keeps appearing in Irish Christmas gift guides.
